A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoR framework, MPM dataset, PPT training strategy and SMPS inference procedure. The complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables and equations, support reliable comparison and matching of relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoR evaluations on MATH, GSM8K and miniF2F, training-stage and paradigm-order ablations, model-scaling experiments, and appendix majority-voting results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds competition-benchmark results and expanded model-scaling comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the dataset construction procedure, three-stage PPT, training loss, task-dependent paradigm sequences and SMPS. Testing additional model sizes does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 1 expand evaluation to AMC2023 and AIME2024 contest problems, alongside the retained MATH, GSM8K and miniF2F benchmarks. This substantially broadens the evaluated competition datasets, although the broad arithmetic/theorem-proving task categories and training sources remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds explicit DeepSeekMath-Instruct-7B and DeepSeekMath-RL-7B comparison rows, absent from v1's corresponding table despite textual mentions. Table 5 adds unmodified Qwen2.5-Math and Llama-3.1 controls within the scaling comparison. The established theorem-proving comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added AMC2023 and AIME2024 evaluations use Maj@64 on 40 and 30 problems, respectively; the scaling study adds a 70B configuration and base-model controls. Existing training settings and main miniF2F budgets remain unchanged. Table 5's Pass@1 caption leaves its miniF2F setting unclear because it repeats a Llama base score labeled Pass@128 in Table 1.

E4.justification: Table 5 substantially expands the scaling analysis from two CoR Qwen sizes on arithmetic benchmarks to base-versus-CoR comparisons across Qwen and Llama models, reaching 70B and including theorem proving. The PPT-stage, paradigm-order, leakage and majority-voting analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new Maj@64 setting concerns inference aggregation rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New results include CoR's 34/40 on AMC2023 and 12/30 on AIME2024, additional baseline scores, and expanded scaling results, including Llama-3.1-70B CoR scores of 70.7 on MATH and 90.0 on GSM8K. Original CoR benchmark scores remain unchanged. Section 5.1.1 revises the stated miniF2F margin over DeepSeek-Math-Base from 14.0 to 37.7 points.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation of CoR, training loss and SMPS, including Equations 1–6, is unchanged. No new formal assumption, theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the 41.0-point theorem-proving comparison from GPT-4 to GPT-4o and the stated arithmetic advantage over RL methods from 7.9 to 15.0 points. The introduction instead highlights a 24.2-point MATH advantage over GPT-4. The central unified-reasoning, PPT and zero-shot-generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.2.1 adds an explanation that PPT stage two refines computational precision and NLR–AR collaboration despite prior code exposure. New Appendix B.3 discusses risks from unvetted Python libraries and inherited model biases, with deployment qualifications. Existing interpretations of paradigm ordering and reasoning hierarchy are retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies dataset-source references for the added contests and SFT sample counts of 776k and 920k for the added DeepSeekMath-Instruct and RL rows. Existing prompts, curation rules and training hyperparameters are unchanged. Appendix A.6 mostly relocates information already present in v1's Table 3.

R1.justification: v2 adds two AI-MO dataset references and citations to Kong et al. on model bias and Yu et al. on ethical alignment. The related-work discussion and positioning against single-paradigm reasoning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction's experimental summary and several results paragraphs are condensed or rewritten. Author/contact information changes, and Appendices A.6 and B.3 are introduced. The main section order and most method and discussion prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Central result displays are substantially restructured: Table 1 gains contest columns, Table 5 becomes a grouped base/CoR scaling comparison, and v1's resource-rich Table 3 becomes a compact main table plus expanded Appendix Table 7. Figures 2 and 3 are redrawn with revised icons and linework. The original majority-voting table is retained as Table 8.

improvement.justification: The contest evaluations and base-controlled scaling study provide useful additional support for CoR's generality, while revised headline comparisons align better with reported tables. However, new inconsistencies limit confidence: Section 5.1.1 gives Llama-Instruct contest counts of 16 and 5, versus 10 and 0 in Table 1, and Table 5 leaves miniF2F sampling unclear. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
